Subject: Lumen Health — evaluation sprint & capacity handshake

Hi Samira — great to connect earlier. Attached is an initial mutual action plan (Lumen_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a short CSV with the capacity assumptions I used. Quick summary and asks so we can lock an evaluation runway that maps to a reservation milestone: 

- Proposed eval sprint: 2 weeks (canary) + 2 weeks (full eval) starting late-April.
- Expected workload (please confirm): ~10k inference calls / month, peaks ~3 concurrent live sessions, average sequence length ~350 tokens.
- Target deployment: Private (VPC) but we want a Dedicated staging for the canary.

Asks: 
1) Can you confirm procurement contact and rough PO lead time? (CC'd procurement alias in follow-up please)
2) Can you confirm whether 3 concurrent sessions is a realistic peak? If this grows to 8–10x we should re-size.
3) Any data residency or HSM/KMS controls we should account for?

We capture the key milestone dates in the MAP: evaluation start, evaluation signoff, reserved-capacity commitment (DocuSign link in final MAP), and provisioning checkpoints. For transparency, I attached our SOC2 snapshot.

If the timeline and sizing look reasonable I can loop in Marissa to formalize the reservation options (tranches / canary cards) and Vivek to confirm provisioning lead times.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow if useful.

— Chloe
Chloe Martin
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Samira Patel <samira.patel@lumenhealth.com>

Cc: Procurement Lumen <procurement@lumenhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lumen Health — evaluation sprint & capacity handshake

Thanks Chloe — this looks like a helpful starting point. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement: I’ve CC'd our procurement mailbox (procurement@lumenhealth.com). Typical internal PO lead time is 4–6 weeks if there are no contract redlines; if we require special terms it can extend to ~8 weeks.
- Workload: The 10k/month estimate is our initial projection. Peak concurrency at launch is actually closer to 5 sessions; we expect load to ramp to ~15 sessions over the next 3 months if the pilot succeeds.
- Residency/KMS: We require the private deployment to be within our US-only VPC and to use our KMS (customer-managed).

Questions for Redwood: 
1) Lead times: what are your typical provisioning windows for Dedicated reserved capacity vs a Private on-prem/VPC package? (we need to map procurement dates to provisioning dates)
2) If we commit to a tranche (e.g., an initial 2-card canary then add 6 cards), can you stagger delivery and billing?

I’ll review the MAP with our PM and loop back with concrete dates. We’d like to avoid a procurement signature that lands before provisioning lead time is realistic.

— Samira
Samira Patel
Head of ML Platforms
Lumen Health
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Lumen Health — evaluation sprint & capacity handshake

Marissa / Vivek — forwarding Samira's reply (below). TL;DR: customer wants US-only VPC, customer-managed KMS, initial expected peak 5 concurrent (ramp to ~15), procurement lead time 4–8 weeks. They want staggered delivery (canary then bulk).

From my sizing sketch I recommended: 
- Canary: 2 x A100s (or 2 x H100 L4/80GB equiv for lower latency) for a 2-week canary to validate KV/prefix caching and latency SLOs.
- Eval-phase pool: add 6 additional cards (total 8) for the full 4-week evaluation to simulate traffic overhead and concurrency.
- Production tranche: ability to add another 8–12 cards if they hit the 10–15 concurrent range.

Can you confirm the following feasibility/lead-time assumptions so I can update the MAP and provide specific dates to Samira: 
1) Dedicated reserved capacity provisioning (on our managed cluster in us-west): typical lead time for partial delivery (canary cards first) — I estimate 6–10 weeks; confirm if we can expedite the canary in 2 weeks.
2) Private VPC package (deploy into customer VPC via private control plane): lead time 12–20 weeks depending on KMS integration and networking approvals.
3) Staggered billing: confirm finance supports tranche billing keyed to card acceptance.

Also flagging that procurement timeline might push the DocuSign/commit date later — if procurement takes 6–8 weeks provisioning must be scheduled accordingly so customer isn't waiting.

— Chloe

Hi Samira / Procurement team — thanks for the details and for looping procurement in. We updated the MAP (attached: Lumen_MAP_v1.xlsx -> Lumen_MAP_v2 in the shared link) to reflect: 

Milestones & proposed dates (draft):
- Evaluation kickoff (canary): 2027-05-03 — 2 weeks on 2 cards (canary).
- Full evaluation: 2027-05-17 — 2 weeks on 8-card eval pool.
- Evaluation signoff: 2027-05-31 (decision point).
- Commitment & DocuSign: target signature 2027-06-07 (aligns to procurement lead time of 3–6 weeks).
- Provisioning checkpoint (initial cards live): 2027-06-21.

What we can commit to operationally: 
- Dedicated managed path (us-west): we can provision the canary within 2 weeks if the deal team approves an expedited staging allocation; full 8-card eval pool typically requires 6–10 weeks from signed commitment for guaranteed capacity.
- Private VPC: our delivery estimate is 12–18 weeks post-signature when KMS integration and customer firewall rules are standard; variability depends on KMS vendor and IAM approvals.
- Staggered billing: finance will support tranche billing tied to acceptance milestones; we will provide a billing schedule in the next DocuSign package.

Action items for Procurement / Customer: 
1) Procurement please advise expected internal signature window and any standard SOW redlines.
2) Customer to confirm peak concurrency ramp plan (5 -> 15) so we can add buffer to the eval pool sizing.

Related artifacts we've shared: MAP spreadsheet (Drive link), SOC2 snapshot (attached), and a short capacity-assumptions CSV. I'll drop the DocuSign commitment draft once procurement confirms the signature timeline.

If you want to get a clear procurement-to-provisioning Gantt, I'm happy to run a 30-min sync early next week.

Best — Marissa
